title: Deleted items must be semantically distinct from temporarily unavailable items in availability query
gherkin:
Feature: Availability State Semantics Separation
  Scenario: Deleted item returns permanent non-rentable semantic
    Given an item with ID "item-123" exists in the system
    And the item is marked as deleted
    When I query availability for item "item-123" for period "2024-01-15" to "2024-01-20"
    Then the response must indicate permanent non-rentability
    And the response must NOT use temporary unavailability wording
    And the semantic category must be "PERMANENTLY_NON_RENTABLE" or equivalent
    And the response must NOT conflate the deleted state with maintenance or manual restrictions
rationale: E5, E6, E10 document that current implementation conflates operationally invalid records with temporarily unavailable items. This test ensures deleted items are surfaced with distinct semantic representation that clearly indicates permanent non-rentability rather than temporary blocking.
usedContextItems: System must distinguish between different semantic categories of item non-availability (e.g., deleted/operationally invalid vs. temporarily blocked/maintenance vs. manual restrictions)|Availability query results must clearly differentiate between items that are permanently non-rentable (deleted/invalid) and items that are temporarily unavailable|Deleted items or items with invalid operational status must not be surfaced through the same availability wording as temporarily blocked items
